content.title: About
content.content: Strawberries are aromatic berries of the plant Fragaria × ananassa, cultivated in many temperate regions worldwide. The fruits are sweet, juicy, with a characteristic fragrance and bright red color. Strawberries are eaten fresh, used in desserts, jams, smoothies, and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Strawberries are not true botanical berries; they are an aggregate fruit composed of many tiny seeds on the surface.
There are over 600 strawberry cultivars, differing in flavor, aroma, and harvest time.
Strawberry is a national symbol of both Russia and the United States.
The typical season in the Northern Hemisphere runs from May to July, but greenhouse production makes them available year‑round.
Strawberry fields often use straw mulch to retain soil moisture and suppress weeds.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Strawberries provide a high amount of vitamin C, which supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: The berries contain anthocyanins and flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Dietary fiber in strawberries promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Strawberries have a low energy density, making them a good choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Potassium and folate
items.content: Strawberries are a source of potassium, which helps maintain fluid balance, and folate, essential for cell division.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to strawberries, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Strawberries are often treated with pesticides; washing thoroughly or choosing organic varieties is recommended.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Strawberries can be eaten fresh, added to yogurt, oatmeal, salads, desserts, smoothies, and drinks. They can also be made into jam, sauces, or frozen for later use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store strawberries in the refrigerator in their original packaging or a container lined with a paper towel to absorb moisture. Consume within 2–3 days. Freeze berries for longer storage.
